title: Onboarding checkpoint - legal, billing & KMS flow
summary: Kickoff to align on MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA tiering for reserved capacity, KMS/SSO preflight and verification path. Customer emphasized data residency and audit trail requirements; Redwood team committed to share security pack and a pricing path for a pilot. Next steps include legal redlines, pilot SOW, and a technical dry run for KMS key rotation tests.
topics: Private deployment vs Dedicated vs Hosted

Customer to send primary MSA redlines by 2026-05-10
Schedule KMS dry-run with Novara infra team (Priya/Samr + Ellen) week of 2026-05-11

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: May 2, 2026
- Time: 11:00 AM ET / 08:00 AM PT
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Novara Procurement), Maya (Novara Security), Tom (Novara Legal), Ellen (Novara Platform)

Auto-summary (auto): Align contract path, verify KMS/SSO approach and run pilot pricing options.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I think we've got a decent agenda listed but quick intros?
[00:08] Jordan: Hi Jordan here, procurement. We wanted to make sure we get the MSA timeline nailed down and understand billing impact around dedicated capacity.
[00:15] Maya: Maya, head of security. Main things for us are KMS, audit logs, and data residency, also retention controls.
[00:22] Tom: Tom, legal counsel. We'll likely have some targeted redlines in the DPA around subprocessors and egress fees.
[00:30] Alex: Great, Priya from the infra team will walk through the KMS and deployment options after I run a quick overview.
[00:37] Priya: Hi all, quick one: Redwood has three rails - hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC. For Novara with PHI, we usually see customers pick Dedicated or Private.
[00:49] Ellen: Right, we're leaning dedicated with private control plane but we need SSO and a KMS that's customer-managed. Can Redwood support bringing our AWS KMS or HSM?
[01:00] Priya: Yes, we support customer KMS via external key wrapping and HSM workflows. There is a preflight for key rotation that we run, that's what we'd like to schedule.
[01:11] Maya: Clarify preflight: do you store any plaintext outside the customer's envelope? That was a question in last week's security intake.
[01:18] Priya: No plaintext storage. There can be transient in-memory caches for model KV but they are encrypted at rest, and keys are customer-managed if you opt in. I will note though sometimes docs transcribe as "KV cash" in our templates so forgive any odd wording in the pack.
[01:30] Jordan: On the commercial side we need to understand SLA tiers. For Dedicated we want 99.95 with financial credits and clear ramp clauses.
[01:37] Alex: Yep, standard is 99.9 for hosted and 99.95 for dedicated with an addendum. There are also burst policies. How strict is your must-have for 99.95?
[01:47] Jordan: It's pretty important for our SLAs, though we can accept staged ramping during pilot if the SLA is contractual for production.
[01:55] Tom: We'll look at the indemnity and data processing clauses. Also export-control language; we're in EU and US, so data residency matters.
[02:03] Alex: Understood. We'll flag residency options - region pinning and Private (VPC) deployments.
[02:08] Maya: On audits, we need syslogs with token-level tracing for a six month retention window. Does Redwood's console export that?
[02:17] Samir: We can export trace logs and we have a per-route telemetry retention option; six months is supported under enterprise package. I will include the retention cost line item.
[02:25] Ellen: Also how do you handle data deletion requests? We need to be able to purge user data and have proof of deletion for audits.
[02:33] Priya: We support deletion APIs and can provide deletion receipts. For the KV/cache there is a purge run that takes place; I will demo that in the dry-run.
[02:41] Jordan: Pricing — what is the delta for dedicated versus hosted? We have a rough budget and will need committed throughput numbers.
[02:48] Alex: Ballpark: dedicated reserved pools have a lower per-token unit cost but you pay a monthly capacity fee; hosted is more expensive per token but no reserve. For example, a 3-node reserved pool might tilt costs down by ~30% for heavy steady workloads. We'll include a worked example in the deck.
[02:59] Tom: About DPA: subprocessors list — does Redwood share the cloud providers and any third-party monitoring tools? We need transparency.
[03:07] Alex: Yes, we list primary cloud infra providers and major third-party dependencies in the DPA appendix. For private deployments you keep more control.
[03:15] Maya: Do you provide an SOC2 report and penetration test summary?
[03:19] Alex: Yes SOC2 Type II report is available; we'll share the latest and a redacted pen test summary.
[03:25] Jordan: On the billing mechanism, can you do net 60 and portal invoicing? Our finance team prefers Net 60 with PO processing.
[03:33] Samir: Finance options vary by contract; net 30 is standard but we can escalate for enterprise terms and include Net 60 in the SOW if approved. I will escalate once we have deal size.
[03:43] Ellen: KMS specifics — we use AWS KMS with envelope encryption and key rotation every 90 days. We need to test rotation without downtime.
[03:52] Priya: We do key rotation tests in staging and support seamless rotation if proper wrapping is used. The dry-run will simulate that.
[04:00] Maya: Also curious about retained model artifacts — are intermediate embeddings or prompts persisted? Some vendors persist for tuning.
[04:07] Priya: By default we don't persist user prompts beyond request logs unless customer opts into telemetry for tuning; that's clearly an opt-in. We'll show the telemetry toggle in console.
[04:16] Tom: Legal redlines I expect: egress fee caps, subprocessors, data residency clauses, and SLA credits. We'll send a tracked doc.
[04:24] Alex: Great. Can we agree on dates? We propose Redwood shares security pack and baseline SOW by Tuesday (May 5). Customer to send MSA redlines by May 10. KMS dry-run week of May 11.
[04:35] Jordan: That works, subject to internal calendar.
[04:38] Alex: Any blockers?
[04:40] Maya: One open item: do you support HSM-backed keys for FIPS compliance?
[04:45] Priya: We can integrate with customer HSMs, yes; some configuration work on our side and time for validation. We'll include the HSM playbook in the pack.
[04:54] Ellen: Also want to note data residency - we need EU-only processing for certain datasets. Is model routing region-locking supported?
[05:01] Priya: Yes region pinning is supported for requests; there are minor latency tradeoffs but it's standard capability.
[05:07] Jordan: On commercial thresholds — we might want a pilot of 200k tokens/mo then scale. Need a pricing SKU for that.
[05:14] Alex: We'll include a pilot SKU and an escalation pricing sheet based on committed QPS and token volume.
[05:20] Tom: Question on liability cap — can Redwood align to our standard 1x annual fee for liability?
[05:26] Alex: We typically negotiate liability caps per account tier. We'll have legal discuss and propose a pathway; for pilot stage we can do mutual cap with limited carveouts.
[05:34] Jordan: Also, any competitors we're concerned about? We've evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic; main differentiation is control and observability.
[05:43] Alex: Right, we'll highlight per-token economics and traceability.
[05:47] Samir: I'll own the billing intake and link it to our finance ops.
[05:50] Alex: Cool. Quick recap then we'll close with explicit next steps.
[05:55] Alex: Recap - Redwood sends security pack & pricing by 5/5, Novara sends MSA redlines by 5/10, dry-run KMS week of 5/11, Redwood to provide pilot SOW and billing options.
[06:05] Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[06:08] Tom: Thanks.
[06:10] Maya: Thanks everyone.
meeting_footer: End of transcript. Call ended at 11:54 AM ET.
